affectedPublicSurfaces: demo.app-juli.com `/decisions/in-progress/[executionId]` -- the run route (`apps/demo/src/app/decisions/in-progress/[executionId]/page.tsx`), where the confirmation sheet mounts. This is the FIRST renderer for a decision request: `ux-surface.md` C records that the protocol exists and no component renders it.

The confirmation call from the browser to `api.app-juli.com` -- `POST /v1/demo/runs/{run_id}/confirmations/{tool_call_id}`, reached through `apps/demo/src/lib/agent-event-stream.ts` (whose own header still says nothing under `apps/demo` imports it) and the confirmation transport this slice builds on top of it. The route is NOT changed; it gains its first caller.

`packages/contracts/src/agent-events.ts` -- `proposed_change` is `Record<string, unknown>` today on BOTH `WorkflowApprovalRequiredPayload` and `ConfirmationOptionPayload` (verified in this tree). This slice adds the discriminated `change` shape as a TypeScript narrowing PLUS its runtime validator beside the existing closed-8-member event-union validators. The wire shape does not move; no backend payload producer changes.
`packages/contracts/src/seller-copy.ts` -- the shared banned-pattern guard, applied to every string on the sheet including the decline copy and the expiry reason.

The seam the rest of the epic plugs into: the discriminator dispatch, the confirm/decline transport and the server-driven expiry are built ONCE here and reused by #1781 (`batch`) and #1783 (`report`). A second dispatch, a second transport or a second countdown in a later slice is a design failure this plan is written to prevent.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: vitest (jsdom) component tests run from the worktree root through the workspace filter, so the suite resolves THIS worktree's `apps/demo` and `packages/contracts` and not a stale sibling checkout. Post-deploy: the candidate demo is reached only through the restricted test listener/hostname -- zero public traffic, `candidatePublicTrafficPercent` 0, stable serving 100% -- and the walk is done in a real browser so a missing JS chunk shows up as a broken surface rather than as a green status code.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: apiSideEffectsInScope is TRUE: confirming on the candidate POSTs a confirmation for a replayed run, which appends that option's CAPTURED continuation (ADR-084 d.2) -- a write to the Synthetic shop's own rows and nothing else. No vendor mutation, no production write. workersDisabledOnCandidate stays TRUE: the continuation is served by the demo replay path in the API, not by a Celery worker, so the journey does not need one and ADR-035's no-background-processing rule is honoured.

journeys.name: typed-change-shape-confirm-decline-and-expiry
assertions: pre-merge: a captured `workflow.approval_required` event whose single option's `proposed_change` discriminates as `change` with a LISTING FIELD renders the field name, its before-struck / after-highlighted values and every consequence line FROM THE PAYLOAD; the DISCOUNT variant renders depth, the 30-day window and the >= 1-day hold from the payload's own fields, and mutating any one of them changes the rendering (src/__tests__/confirmation-sheet-change-shape.test.tsx::renders_the_named_write_and_its_consequences_from_the_payload)

pre-merge: confirm posts the payload's own `tool_call_id`, `option_id` and `params_sha` VERBATIM -- asserted on the OUTBOUND REQUEST, never on component state -- and a single interaction authorises nothing: one click sends ZERO requests (S-FR-3's one CONFIRM pause, N = 1) (src/__tests__/confirmation-sheet-change-shape.test.tsx::confirm_posts_the_payloads_own_binding_and_one_click_sends_nothing)

pre-merge: "khong thuc hien" sends a DECLINE and the declined outcome renders as a CHOICE -- no error styling, no failure iconography, no retry control anywhere in the rendered tree (src/__tests__/confirmation-sheet-change-shape.test.tsx::decline_is_a_choice_not_a_failure)

pre-merge: a `proposed_change` whose discriminator the client does not recognise FAILS CLOSED -- it refuses to render a proposal, says so, and arms no confirm control; a partial or blank proposal is the defect (src/__tests__/confirmation-sheet-change-shape.test.tsx::unknown_change_shape_fails_closed)

pre-merge: with a FIXED clock advanced past the payload's `expires_at`, the countdown equals the SERVER's value at every point -- never a client timer seeded at mount -- and input stops being accepted with the reason stated (S-NFR-2's 4 h expiry, `params_sha` binding) (src/__tests__/confirmation-sheet-change-shape.test.tsx::expiry_follows_the_server_and_copy_passes_the_guard)

pre-merge: EVERY seller-facing string this surface renders is collected from the RENDERED tree (not from a hand-listed constant array) and checked against `SELLER_COPY_BANNED_PATTERNS` imported from `packages/contracts/src/seller-copy.ts` -- the shared `packages/contracts/seller-copy-banned-patterns.json` source, never a local copy of the list

pre-merge: every test input is a CAPTURED contract payload -- the golden fixtures in `packages/contracts/src/` and the tool-captured golden scenarios (#1311) -- driven through the real TypeScript contract types. Hand-authored event or envelope JSON is NOT an acceptable input (ADR-084 d.2); a shape the capture tool cannot yet produce is a gap in the tool, not a licence to type one out -- here specifically the golden `workflow.approval_required` fixture in `packages/contracts/src/agent-events.ts` and the captured scenarios

post-deploy: each route below returns HTTP 200 as a RENDERED document on the candidate listener with the replayed scenario loaded -- not a 200 shell whose JS chunk 404s: `/decisions/in-progress/<a concrete replayed run id>` (the run route carrying the sheet); `/decisions` (the entry the run is reached from) -- probed with `discoverFromHtml` so every <script>/<link> the document names is fetched and asserted 200 (ADR-035's build-integrity clause: a green /health and a 200 HTML document have both been true while the app was unusable)

post-deploy: on the candidate, reach a replayed decision request, CONFIRM, and observe the chosen continuation render; then on a SECOND replayed run DECLINE and observe the declined terminal render as a choice, not as a failure

post-deploy: the anonymous door ("Dung thu Demo") is opened on the candidate and the browser network log shows ZERO requests to any `/v1/*` path for the whole walk (ADR-094 d.1) -- the replay is client-side content with no session, no auth.users row and no Postgres write; a single `/v1/*` call from that door fails the release, because it would be the #1283 shape returning
post-deploy: the candidate `/health` and one authenticated runs read are unchanged -- the typed shape is a client-side narrowing of an existing field and adds no response-model field

staticAssetChecks.notes: The sheet, its discriminator dispatch and its expiry logic must be in the BUILT bundle -- the issue's own release-evidence line. A run that reaches a decision request on a bundle missing the sheet is the failure this check exists to catch. Route shapes verified against `apps/demo/src/app/` in this tree on 2026-09-08: the only page.tsx files under /decisions are `decisions/page.tsx`, `decisions/recommendations/[recommendationId]/page.tsx` and `decisions/in-progress/[executionId]/page.tsx`. There is NO `/decisions/in-progress` and NO `/decisions/recommendations` index route -- the In-Progress view is the SAME HTML document at /decisions under the `?tab=in-progress` query param (`recommendations-view.tsx` reads `searchParams.get("tab")`). Earlier plans (#1314, #1318) named those two as routes; probing them as HTML routes would 404 and the probe must not be written that way.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. The typed `change` shape is a CLIENT-SIDE NARROWING of the existing `proposed_change: Record<string, unknown>` field plus a runtime validator; the wire shape, the confirmation route and every persisted row are untouched. This slice's whole diff is under `apps/demo/**` and `packages/contracts/src/**`; it opens no migration file, and the migration numbers for the backend slices it depends on are RESERVED BY META and never read from head. If a test cannot pass without a column or an endpoint, the dependency is unmet and the answer is to stop and report, not to write a migration or a second route. Stable and candidate are compatible because the previous bundle simply does not render the new surface, and the rows and routes it reads are unchanged by this slice.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge; discard the candidate and keep the retained previous bundle serving 100%. Nothing is stranded: today no component renders a decision request at all, so the pre-cutover state is the current state.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the retained previous demo bundle. The sheet is additive on the client. The assertion that must hold: a run that reaches a decision request WITHOUT the sheet degrades to a readable waiting state, never a blank screen and never a silently stuck run -- verify by opening such a run on the rolled-back bundle, not by reading a status code.
rollbackAssertion.notes: The PREVIOUS demo bundle is RETAINED and stays serving 100% of public traffic until the candidate passes; rollback is redeploying that retained bundle. Rollback is NOT automatic for this slice: the failure modes here are visual and structural (a surface that renders blank, a chunk that 404s), which a health probe does not catch, so a human reads the candidate journey and decides. No schema step is involved in either direction.

doNotInfer: Do NOT add a surface. v1's seller surfaces are the seven S-FR-1 names -- card, plan review, confirmation sheet, run view, completion message + exception list, notification centre, deadline list -- plus the single deadline view added by the owner waiver of 2026-09-05 (#1790, and ONLY #1790). A slice that believes it needs an eighth surface, a new tab, a new modal shell or a new route is a signal the routing or the design is wrong: STOP AND REPORT, do not build it.

Do NOT hand-author event or envelope JSON, anywhere, for any reason. ADR-084 d.2 forbids it: a second hand-maintained source drifts from the first while both suites stay green -- the defect class behind six W3 post-merge fixes. Test inputs are the captured contract payloads and the tool-captured golden scenarios (#1311). ADR-094 d.5 relaxes this ONLY for the existing client replay in `mock-data.ts`, which this slice neither extends nor imitates.

Do NOT write English seller-facing copy. Vietnamese only, second person ("ban"), per S-NFR-4 and S-NFR-12; there is no EN toggle in v1 (`ux-surface.md` F.12 option (a)). An English label, an English empty state, an English error, or an English tooltip is a defect even when it never ships to a Vietnamese seller in the demo walk.

Do NOT let an internal identifier reach seller-facing text. No `workflow_key`, tool name, playbook key, predicate or guard name, stop-reason identifier, `subject_ref`, run id, order id, SKU id or warehouse id in any rendered string (ADR-084 d.5, S-NFR-4). The banned-pattern guard is the floor, not the ceiling: an identifier the regex list happens not to match is still a defect.

Do NOT read the workflow's identity from anything but the seller-facing envelope. Grouping, gating and labelling derive from `recommendation.workflow_name` and the `is_executable` discriminator that `packages/contracts/src/decisions.ts` already carries; `workflow_key` is absent from that envelope by ADR-084 d.3 and must NOT be reintroduced, inferred, reverse-engineered from a title, or smuggled in through a URL segment. If a v1 workflow cannot be distinguished without leaking the taxonomy, STOP AND REPORT (#1793).

Do NOT render a value outside a numeric field's validated range, and do NOT invent the range. Bounds come from the contract descriptor (`packages/contracts/src/review.ts`), never from a component literal; CE-FR-4's stock goal is `0 <= goal < sellable` and RI-NFR-3 forbids a write below the committed quantity. A control that can express an out-of-range value -- an unclamped slider, a free-text number, a spinner without bounds -- is the defect, whether or not a validator catches it afterwards (#1783).

Do NOT change a backend route, response model, payload producer or database row from this slice. Domain is ui-ux, one domain per issue; the producers are named in the issue's Blocked-by list. Do NOT open `apps/dashboard/`, `ios/`, `backend/src/juli_backend/ai/`, `backend/src/juli_backend/workers/` or the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051) -- this epic's doNotLoad list.

Do NOT prove a contract with a `**kwargs` double or a hand-rolled stub of a contract type. Bind every test collaborator to the REAL exported type and the REAL module; a double proves routing, never that the real payload would render. Consumer-without-producer is the failure this wave exists to prevent.

Do NOT build the `batch` shape (#1781), the `report` shape or its numeric field (#1783), or any multi-option picker beyond N = 1. #1317's picker keeps its Optimize Product case; this is the single-proposal sheet.
Do NOT compose a consequence line, a reversibility statement or a rationale client-side. Every line comes from the payload; a client-composed sentence is a promise no server made (S-NFR-1).
Do NOT seed a countdown from a client clock at mount. The expiry is the server's `expires_at`; a locally seeded timer drifts and then lies about consent.
Do NOT add a lever. This sheet renders what the run PROPOSES: never cancel an order, never write a base price, never write stock below a committed quantity, and never offer a control that could.
Do NOT recompute or re-derive `params_sha` client-side. It is posted back verbatim.
